notes: Cross-verse head consistency. This chapter renders a comparative מִן by two English words twice: *rather than* at ECC.6.5, headed on *than*, and *more than* here, headed on *more*. Nothing in the source licenses the difference — both are a supplied degree word beside the relational word — so one of the two is wrong. Rule 24 heads a multi-word preposition on the token carrying the lexeme rather than the connective, and in a comparative that is *than*, which states the relation, while *more* is what English spends on the degree; the corpus aligns מִן to *more than* headed on *than* in 25 units and to a bare *than* in 119. The head moves from t007 to t008. Every edge, status and source head is as the verse pass returned it.
